botany.native_range: The south-eastern and south-central United States: the coastal plain, the Mississippi and lower Ohio valleys, and parts of Mexico.
botany.habitat: Wet ground. Grows in swamps, floodplains and along river margins where the roots stand in standing water for part of the year.
botany.climate: Humid subtropical to warm temperate, with a substantial annual rainfall and periodic flooding.
distinguishing_characteristics: A tall, straight, columnar trunk with reddish-brown, fibrous, furrowed bark.
A broad, irregular crown of fine-textured, feathery foliage.
Flared buttresses at the base, often with conspicuous vertical ridges.
Cypress knees: conical projections of root that rise above the water around an old tree.
Deciduous unlike most conifers: the needles turn russet and fall in autumn.
interesting_facts: It is one of the few conifers that sheds its needles, which is where the name 'bald' comes from.
The buttresses and knees are thought to help the tree stand in waterlogged, poorly aerated soil.
The wood is famously resistant to rot, which is why it was widely used for pilings and fences.
botany.attribution: Botanical summary compiled for Arboretum. Verify against the Kew Plants of the World Online record for Taxodium distichum before treating any specific figure as authoritative.

assets.note: Mangrove blocks stand in for cypress because they are the only vanilla block with a distinct, root-like state. The resource pack retextures them pale so they read as cypress rather than mangrove. See docs/distribution.md.
